messages:
joe_cust: Hey team — seeing intermittent 429s from the UI when I call the playground generate endpoint. Happens ~1/10 requests, no pattern. Sample request-id in the response header: rwd-7f9c2b. Browser: Chrome on macOS.
Maya (Support): Sorry you're hitting that. Can you grab a HAR + console logs for one of the failing attempts and attach here? Also include the exact request-id from the response header and the time (UTC). That helps correlate with infra traces.
joe_cust: OK working on it. Any specific steps for Chrome? I'm not super familiar with devtools.
Maya (Support): Quick checklist — Chrome (works similarly in Edge):
1) Open DevTools (Cmd+Option+I) -> Network tab. Check "Preserve log".
2) Click the record button (red) if not recording. Reproduce the error.
3) After the 429 appears, right-click the network list -> Save all as HAR with content -> Attach here.
4) Console tab -> right-click -> Save as -> Attach (or copy/paste the console errors).
5) Note the response headers for the failing request (especially: x-request-id, date, status, content-type) and the exact local time you reproduced.
6) If you used an incognito window or have extensions, try once in Incognito with extensions disabled.

Include a minimal curl repro too (we can redact tokens):
```
curl -v "https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED_TOKEN>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"input":"hello"}'
```
If the UI includes special cookies or a session header, export those and attach (we only need them for repro; you can redact secrets when uploading).
Alex (SRE): When you attach the HAR please point out the failing request entry (we look for x-request-id header and status 429). If you can't find x-request-id in the response headers, open the failing request -> Response Headers -> copy any request-id-like header. We use those to pull logs.
joe_cust: Uploaded har and console.txt to the ticket (link: https://support.redwood.ai/upload/abc). HAR filename: 1960000123_capture.har. Failing request id in headers: rwd-7f9c2b. Time: 2025-11-07T18:22:31Z.
Priya (Helpdesk): Thanks — confirming we received the upload. Quick extra asks:
- Can you reproduce consistently if you open DevTools -> Network -> Throttling -> No throttling? (Some extensions add throttling)
- Try once with an Incognito window to rule out extension interference.
joe_cust: Reproduced in Incognito too. Same x-request-id.
Maya (Support): Good. A few more platform-specific tips in case others run into this:
- Safari: Enable Develop menu (Safari -> Preferences -> Advanced -> Show Develop menu). Develop -> Show Web Inspector -> Network -> right-click -> Export HAR. Console -> Save Page Source or copy errors.
- Edge: DevTools same as Chrome -> Preserve log -> Save as HAR.
- If you use macOS and want to capture full console logs including extension stack traces: Console app -> Filter for process: "Chrome" -> export for the time range.
Alex (SRE): For our side, we will search logs for the x-request-id and time window ±2 minutes to see rate-limiting decisions and upstream queues. If that id isn't present, we ask for the HAR entry as JSON and we can extract the request headers.
joe_cust: Do you need browser versions / OS exact strings?
Maya (Support): Yes please — those help. Send user agent string (right-click request -> Headers -> Request Headers -> user-agent) and exact browser version from About page.
joe_cust: Adding UA: Mozilla/5.0 (Macintosh; Intel Mac OS X 13_6) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/120.0.0.0 Safari/537.36
Maya (Support): Perfect. Also if you can run a curl that mimics the failing request and paste output with -v that shows response headers, that'll speed up triage. Example to include the request-id header if present in response:
```
curl -i -v "https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED_TOKEN>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"input":"test"}'
```
Look for lines like:
```
< HTTP/2 429
< date: Fri, 07 Nov 2025 18:22:31 GMT
< x-request-id: rwd-7f9c2b
```
Priya (Helpdesk): Once we have the HAR + console + curl output we'll create an incident trace and ping @Alex for SRE correlation. If you prefer secure upload instead of the ticket link, we can share a short-lived pre-signed URL.
joe_cust: Uploaded the curl output and UA. Anything else I can include?
Maya (Support): One last thing — if you can reproduce and are comfortable, record a short screen capture showing the steps and the DevTools console/network selection. That often saves back-and-forth. If not, the HAR + console + curl are enough.
support-bot: Incident created: INC-20251107-789. Linked logs auto-picked x-request-id: rwd-7f9c2b.
Alex (SRE): I'll take it from here, searching rate-limit keys and policy decisions for that request id. Expect an update within 2 business hours.
joe_cust: Thanks — appreciate the quick help :thumbsup:
